answer:
Safe mode rejects inline JavaScript. It does not turn off JavaScript in general, and the retrieved context doesn't show that it was added in 0.125.0.

- The CLI option reference says: "Reject inline JavaScript assertions and shared transforms." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
- The JavaScript assertions doc gives more detail: "Use `promptfoo eval --safe-mode` or `PROMPTFOO_SAFE_MODE=true` to reject string-based JavaScript assertions and inline expressions handled by the shared transform helper." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md]
- Rejected assertions and transforms fail visibly: "Rejected assertions fail with an explanatory reason; rejected transforms produce an error." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md]
- Some JavaScript still works. The same doc says "JavaScript function values passed through the Node API remain supported." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md] It also says to move rejected expressions into reviewed `file://` scripts.
- It is not a sandbox. The doc warns: "This option is not a sandbox and does not make untrusted configurations safe to run." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md] The text is cut off after "File callbacks, programmatic functions, executable providers, config modules, [...]", so I can't list everything else it leaves enabled.

The 0.125.0 changelog excerpts I have (Features and part of Bug Fixes) don't mention safe mode. The docs describe the feature, but I can't confirm from this context which release introduced it.
